newsitem.title: CHINA: China to set pace on raising HK Telecom stake -C&W.
newsitem.headline: China to set pace on raising HK Telecom stake -C&W.

text.p: The timing for China to increase its stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd was up to Beijing, Cable & Wireless Plc said on Friday.
C&W chief executive Richard Brown said China had "embraced" Hongkong Telecom through investments by China Telecom (Hong Kong) Ltd and a unit of China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd.

"The next move must be under the direction of China," Brown told reporters after Hongkong Telecom's annual meeting on Friday. "It's entirely up to China how they proceed with that, how rapidly they're able to accomplish that."
Hongkong Telecom chairman Brian Smith earlier told the annual meeting: "China Telecom has indicated that it may increase its stake in the coming months."
Last month C&W, which held 59 percent of Hongkong Telecom, said it was selling 5.5 percent to China Telecom for US$1.185 billion, and that further divestments are expected.
China Telecom is controlled by Telpo Communications Ltd, an arm of China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, and is expected to list shares in Hong Kong in the future.

C&W said it was prepared to sell more Hongkong Telecom shares to China Telecom -- with a view to the two becoming equal owners in the Hong Kong company -- if such a move enhanced shareholder value and important projects in China were realised.
That comment has generated regular speculation of further sell downs by C&W of its Hongkong Telecom stake.
Brown, also deputy chairman of Hongkong Telecom, praised China Telecom, which he described as a shell company into which China would inject assets in the form of Chinese projects.
"It is a very clever and creative vehicle with which to get financing by taking advantage of the Hong Kong equity market," Brown said.
He said C&W would consider swapping Hongkong Telecom shares for equity in China Telecom (Hong Kong) in future selldowns.
"It could be in cash but we've expressed an interest in being an equity partner in China Telecom (Hong Kong)," he said.
"One of the elements of the agreement announced last month is that Cable & Wireless has the opportunity to be the largest foreign investor in China Telecom (Hong Kong)."
The China Telecom deal followed the purchase by China Everbright, controlled by China's State Council, of a 7.74-percent stake in Hongkong Telecom from CITIC Pacific Ltd for HK$11.4 billion.
Hong Kong reverted to Chinese rule at midnight (1600 GMT) on June 30.
